## Personal info in a nutshell
I'm a physicist who builds AI systems for a living. Here's my story:
* Born and raised in NCR, India. Delhi native, I live in SF.
* Physicist by instinct, engineer by training. Caltech Applied Physics was my attempt to split the difference. It worked — mostly...
* Spent years deploying AI at scale — petabytes of data, millions of users — at Orbital Insight, IBM Research, Intel, and others.
* Now Chief Scientist at [EnCharge AI](https://enchargeai.com), a Series B startup building analog in-memory computing chips that deliver 10-20x energy efficiency over GPUs for AI inference.
* Write [AI Afterhours](https://aiafterhours.substack.com) — a newsletter about the full stack of AI efficiency.

<div class="about-section">
## My current hypotheses
* The AI energy crisis is already underway — we're just not calling it that yet. Within this decade, power constraints will become the primary bottleneck on AI scaling, ahead of compute and data.
* Published efficiency gains are systematically overstated. Benchmark conditions and production conditions diverge enough that most claimed improvements fail to transfer at real utilization rates.
* The next competitive moat in AI infrastructure will belong to teams that can co-design hardware and software simultaneously — not hand off between them.
* Quantization is underutilized as a research lever and over-relied on as a deployment fix. The gap between what's theoretically achievable and what ships in production is large and largely unacknowledged.
* Transformer attention has a fundamental scaling problem that architectural iteration alone won't resolve. The field will be forced to confront this sooner than current roadmaps assume.
* If you measure AI progress in gigawatts, you are measuring the wrong thing. Energy consumed per useful inference operation is the metric that will matter.
* Production performance and benchmark performance are measuring different systems. Most efficiency claims don't survive the translation.
* Physics sets the floor on energy requirements regardless of software cleverness. The joules required are the joules required — and that constraint will increasingly shape what gets built.
</div>
